Independent sweep (beads-worker-2, 2026-09-09, current main) found ADDITIONAL sites that correlate a node identity with the LOW 64 BITS of an IPv6 address — valid under the rejected native SHA-512 profile (addr[8:16]==SHA512-IID) but INVALID now that routable addresses are upstream AddrForKey:

PRODUCTION CODE:
1. lichen-node/src/node.rs:748 — source[8..] == *sender_iid (sender-identity vs IPv6 source correlation).
2. lichen-node/src/node.rs:387 — iid = origin[8..] extracted from a routable origin.
3. lichen-node/src/secure.rs:1933 — sender_iid from header.src.0[8..].
4. lichen-node/src/rpl_stack/secure.rs:143 — peer_matches_destination: dst.0[8..] == peer_iid.
5. lichen-node/src/routing/gradient.rs:178,318 — destination[8..] treated as IID.
6. lichen-node/src/announce.rs — multiple sites build/compare destinations via destination[8..].copy_from_slice(&iid) (lines ~232,1003,1194,1385,1481); verify whether the destination is a link-local (IID-valid) or routable (AddrForKey) address at each site.

TEST-SUPPORT (breaks ~15 routing::tests DAO tests on current main — observed while reproducing on a stale tree; current main may already fail these if those tests run):
7. lichen-node/src/routing/router.rs:711 — #[cfg(test)] identity recovery via identity.iid == packet_source[8..]; must match ygg_addr_from_pubkey(identity.pubkey) == packet_source instead (or pass the seed explicitly).

Each site needs the same review as mjm7's list: is the address a link-local (SHA-512 IID remains valid per settled decision) or the routable /128 (must correlate via full AddrForKey == address)?
